EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A compact upper level low pressure system tracked across New Mexico and West Texas from the morning to afternoon on the second. Strong forcing for ascent with this system combined with a dryline in the Rolling Plains and abundant instability generated isolated thunderstorms in the extreme southeastern Texas Panhandle into western Oklahoma. One of these storms became severe in eastern Childress County producing quarter size hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A public report was received of quarter size hail west of Kirkland.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms moved across the Brazos Valley and Piney Woods area, producing hail and wind damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: An emergency manager reported multiple trees down west of Austonio. A secondary roof over a trailer house was reported to be blown off. Based on the damage reported, wind speeds were estimated to be 74 mph.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A stalled cold front along the Pecos River Valley and an approaching upper-level disturbance resulted in scattered showers and thunderstorms along and ahead of this front. A few stronger thunderstorms developed around the higher terrain of the Davis Mountains.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Received a phone call of quarter size hail 8 miles south of Alpine along State Highway 118. Time is estimated from radar.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cluster of storms in La Salle County progressed southeastward through the evening hours. These storms intensified and developed into a well-organized MCS with a maturing bow echo feature as it extended into northeastern Duval and Jim Wells counties. An uptick in radar velocity was noted beginning north of San Diego, TX around 8:45pm CDT, with large wet melting hail enforcing a notable stronger surge of northwesterly winds on the southern edge of the storm over west Alice shortly after 9:00pm CDT.||This southern edge of the MCS became the most destructive bowing segment through the rest of the storm's lifespan, resulting in numerous power and transmission poles snapped, metal building structure collapses, and large trees snapped and uprooted. Widespread wind speeds of 70-90 mph were noted, particularly from Alice to Petronila with a few locations seeing wind gusts as high as 115 mph. While we were unable to access the Petronila area to assess the damage further due to numerous downed power and transmission line, photos and videos shared with us suggest that winds in excess of 100 mph continued through this area as well.||Hundreds of power and transmission poles were snapped between Alice and Petronila. Most were snapped near the base, however a few were found to be snapped 10-15 feet above ground, indicating peak winds of 115 mph. In addition, roof damage was observed, along with several rolled over semi-trucks and campers. Overall, the preliminary path length is 54 miles with a max width of 16 miles.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: There were 80 transmission lines blown down upon survey. Time estimated from radar.
